title: Amma Theodora
hookLine: she says humility, not fasting, is what defeats the demons
tomorrow: is keeping quiet the same as being honest?

cards: Step counts, personal bests, streaks, rankings: some things are easy to measure. A desert mother tells a story about someone who measured.
There was a hermit who could drive out demons, and one day he asked them straight: what makes you leave? Is it fasting? Is it keeping vigil, awake all night in prayer?
Is it living far from everyone? Those are the obvious guesses. The demons give him a different answer, and it's the one thing that never shows up on a scoreboard.

teach.b: The story comes from Amma Theodora. Is it fasting that drives you out? No, say the demons.
We don't eat or drink at all. Is it the vigils? No.
We never sleep. Is it living apart from the world? No.
We live in the deserts already. Then what sends you away?
Nothing overcomes us, they say, but humility. And Theodora turns to her listeners: do you see how humility wins? Here's the turn in it.

Every practice the hermit names, the demons can match and outdo. In this story they're the best fasters in the desert, a detail worth passing on. Discipline on its own is something they're already good at.
What they can't do is be humble. So that's the answer to yesterday's question. Theodora doesn't throw out fasting and prayer.
They just can't win by themselves.
The letter to the Philippians gives humility a shape: "Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves."
Lowliness of mind isn't thinking you're nothing. It's thinking of the other person first, and it usually looks small: a dish, a door, a credit passed along.

how: Christians in monastic and church traditions alike treat humility as a virtue to practice, and the desert mothers' sayings, Theodora's among them, are read for guidance on it.

o: a desert mother whose demons fear only humility
a desert town where the hermits gathered
an empress who ruled from Constantinople

games.q: what drives them out — tap the pairs.
p: asked the demons what drives them out
we don't eat or drink at all

s: in Theodora's story, long fasting is what drives the demons out
the demons say they never eat at all. only humility overcomes them.
the popular version. Philippians says esteem others better: think of them first.
Theodora keeps fasting and prayer, but says they can't win alone
the demons outdo both. humility is the one thing they can't do.

games.q: your group project gets praised, and the teacher names only you. the quiet kid did half the research. what fits Theodora's story?
o: say nothing; correcting a teacher in class looks proud.
name the quiet kid's work out loud, so the credit lands.
insist you did the least, so nobody thinks you're proud.
games.why: Philippians: esteem others better than yourselves. not putting yourself down; putting them first.

practice: Get up and do one small unseen thing with your hands: rinse a cup that isn't yours, or straighten the shoes by the door. Do it slowly, and notice the warm water, the weight of each shoe, the quiet.
Then sit back down and tell no one.

wordCard.voice: Amma Theodora. A desert mother who told of demons that could fast and keep vigil, but could not be humble.

orig.note: Greek: lowliness of mind, humility, in Philippians 2:3.

carryVoice: Hold on to this: humility wins, and it starts with thinking of the other first. See you tomorrow.
